newsitem.title: USA: Brazil gets $947.8 mln in four IADB loans.
newsitem.headline: Brazil gets $947.8 mln in four IADB loans.

text.p: The Inter-American Development Bank (IADB) has signed four contracts giving Brazil $947.8 million in loans for economic and social development projects, the bank said Sunday.
The contracts were signed by IADB president Enrique Iglesias and Brazil's Treasurer Luiz Carlos Sturzenegger in Barcelona, where the IADB annual meeting opens Monday.
One $500 million loan will be used to help modernize the fiscal administration in Brazil's 26 states and the federal district, the IADB said in a statement released in Washington.
A second loan for $350 million would help improve health services and widen coverage among low-income groups, including efforts to increase disease prevention.

A third loan for $78 million would help modernize Brazil's federal tax system and strengthen the Federal Revenue Secretariat, improving collection of tax revenues and reducing the costs of foreign trade operations, the IADB said.

The fourth loan, for $19.8 million would help reduce destructive flooding in the city of Campinas by financing construction of drainage facilities like storm sewers, as well as building better housing for residents in flood-prone areas.
The terms of the loans were not immediately available.
